notes:
SOURCE. English Wiktionary, read from the kaikki.org machine extraction (https://kaikki.org/dictionary/Chinese), extracted 2026-08-28 from the enwiktionary dump of 2026-08-05. Every row's sourceUrl is the Wiktionary page that renders the transcription; `sourceIpa` is Wiktionary's IPA string verbatim, so every conversion described below can be re-derived from the row itself. Nothing here was generated by a tool or a model - the repo's chinese-to-pinyin / to-jyutping / es-hangul packages were not used as a source for any field.

VARIETY. Standard Cantonese (Guangzhou / Hong Kong) only: Wiktionary sounds tagged Cantonese + Guangzhou + Sinological-IPA with the raw tag Standard-Cantonese. Rejected: Taishan, Dongguan, Yangjiang and Nanning readings, and every non-Cantonese topolect on the same headword. Cantonese lives inside en.wiktionary's Chinese entries, so sourceUrl points at the Chinese section.

TONE NOTATION, AND A DIVERGENCE THAT MATTERS. Wiktionary writes tone with Unicode SUPERSCRIPT digits (/nei̯¹³ hou̯³⁵/); each digit was rewritten to its Chao tone letter (1=˩ 2=˨ 3=˧ 4=˦ 5=˥) - a re-encoding of the same values, not a re-transcription. Wiktionary's Guangzhou readings use TONE 2 = 35 and TONE 5 = 13, whereas Wikipedia's Help:IPA/Cantonese key gives 25 and 23 for those same two tones. This file follows Wiktionary throughout and is internally consistent; a position-wise exact comparison against the Wikipedia key would mark every tone-2 and tone-5 syllable wrong. Tones 1/3/4/6 agree with the key (55, 33, 21, 22), and checked (entering-tone) syllables carry the single-digit level tones 5 / 3 / 2, so ˥ ˧ ˨ on a syllable closed by p̚ t̚ k̚ is correct and not a truncated contour.

THE IPA IS REAL IPA, NOT JYUTPING SPELLING - the specific failure being measured. It uses ɐ vs aː, ɵ, œ, ɪ, ʊ, ŋ, kʷ labialisation, ː length and ̚ unreleased stops. 廣東 is kʷɔːŋ˧˥ tʊŋ˥˥, never "gwong2 dung1". `romanization` is separately Jyutping: Wiktionary renders its tone digits as superscripts, converted here to ASCII digits (the Jyutping convention), with the changed-tone marker written as a hyphen, e.g. maa1-4.

CHANGED TONE (變調) is Cantonese's analogue of sandhi and is marked the same way, with a superscript minus in the source. Those rows carry `sandhi: true`, `sandhiTypes: ["changed-tone"]`, `ipaCitation` for the underlying tones, and the Jyutping keeps the hyphenated form. 83 of 350 rows are marked. Common examples: 電話 din6 waa6-2, 廣東話 gwong2 dung1 waa6-2, 醫院 ji1 jyun6-2.

SYLLABIC NASALS. 唔 (m̩˨˩), 五 (ŋ̍˩˧) and their compounds have a syllabic nasal as their only nucleus, so they contain no vowel symbol. Those 4 rows carry `syllabicNasal: true` so a harness that hard-requires a vowel can exclude them. They are correct Cantonese, not defects, and 唔 is too central to the language to leave out.

SYMBOL INVENTORY vs Help:IPA/Cantonese (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Cantonese). Beyond the tone values above, Wiktionary adds tie bars on affricates (t͡s, t͡sʰ), the non-syllabic diacritic on offglides (ei̯, ou̯, ɐu̯), explicit ː length, ̚ on unreleased final stops, and ɪ / ʊ as the allophones of i / u before velars. The consonant and vowel inventories otherwise match the key.

VALIDATION. Every row's Jyutping was checked programmatically against the IPA's underlying tone contour, syllable by syllable (1 = 55/53/5, 2 = 35, 3 = 33/3, 4 = 21/11, 5 = 13, 6 = 22/2); disagreements were dropped rather than guessed. The same check passes on 99.6% of the full Cantonese index. Rows also pass: zero ASCII digits, no enclosing / or [ ], a vowel or syllabic-consonant nucleus, no leftover superscript, deduplicated on `text`.

SCRIPT. `text` is TRADITIONAL, matching the Wiktionary page that carries the pronunciation and matching normal Cantonese orthography. `simplified` carries Wiktionary's own Simplified-Chinese form where it differs (165 rows), for the app's `yue` (simplified-script) code.

SELECTION. Word tier: mine - Cantonese-specific core vocabulary (佢, 唔, 冇, 嘅, 乜嘢, 點解, 屋企, 飲茶), the classic six-tone minimal set on one segment (詩 史 試 時 市 事), checked syllables, ɵ/œ rimes, syllabic nasals, and changed-tone compounds. Sentence tier: 72 hand-picked plus 28 harvested from attested `phrase` / `proverb` headwords, weighted toward genuinely Cantonese expressions (identified by the Cantonese-only characters 哋嘅咗冇唔佢乜嘢咁 喺睇攞嘥啲嚟) rather than shared literary chengyu.

MULTIPLE READINGS. 54 rows carry `ipaAlternatives`: the other attested readings of the same headword, with `romanizationAlternatives` and `sourceIpaAlternatives` positionally aligned to it - index 0 pairs with index 0 throughout. `ipa`, `romanization` and `sourceIpa` remain the PRIMARY reading (the one Wiktionary lists first), and the sandhi fields describe the primary only. An earlier version of this file kept only that first reading; across the curated candidate lists 88 headwords carried more than one attested reading and were silently truncated to one. None were ever REJECTED for having several, and none of the drops were mispairings - the agreement check between romanization and IPA found a consistent pairing for every reading it saw.

WHICH ALTERNATIVES ARE INCLUDED, AND WHY NOT ALL OF THEM. Wiktionary also lists readings no modern speaker uses - 不 fǒu / Fōu / fū / bū, 日 mì, 事 zì, 女 nǜ / rǔ - hanging off senses glossed "alternative form of ...", "original form of ...", "only used in ...", "a surname". A scorer that credits an engine with whichever reading it came closest to would hand out free marks for those, so a reading is kept only when its sound tags carry none of Erhua/dated/obsolete/archaic/nonstandard/rare, its entry has at least one sense NOT marked obsolete/archaic/historical, and the entry's gloss is a definition rather than a cross-reference. Changed-tone jyutping (jan4-2) collapses into its base reading (jan4). For 20 common heteronyms the readings are named explicitly instead of harvested, so the frequent cases are exact rather than exhaustive; every named reading was verified to exist on its page, and the one that did not (大 dài) was removed rather than invented. Elsewhere at most two alternatives are kept, in Wiktionary's own order, and only on the word tier. A stricter harness can ignore the `*Alternatives` fields and score the primary alone.

SENTENCE TIER, AND WHERE IT STOPS. As for Mandarin, Wiktionary transcribes headwords and not running sentences, so the tier is whole expressions: colloquial set phrases, proverbs and 歇後語 of up to 13 characters. The pool of attested, validating Cantonese phrase/proverb headwords is 7418, but only 209 of those contain a Cantonese-only character - the rest are shared written-Chinese expressions read in Cantonese, which are valid but less characteristic. 100 is a chosen cap; the genuinely-Cantonese supply is what would bind first, at roughly 250 rows.
